title: Unchecked Consumers
claim: In the current candidate snapshot, helper and worker read the cursor node fields and follow node->next without validating that a pointer is within the FIFO pool or that it is the expected ring successor; both consume user-writable data_size as a copy bound.

evidence.observation: Reads fifo->state/data_size, copies payload, then loads aw->rtp_ptr->next and stores it as the new cursor; no pointer-range or exact-successor check appears in this function.

evidence.locator: richtap_rtp_work loop around state, node_size, memcpy and fifo->next
evidence.observation: Reads RTP_CURSOR->state/data_size, copies payload and assigns fifo->next to RTP_CURSOR without validation.
Stock loads cursor, state, signed size and next from node + 0x8; bounds trap only covers the legacy count/copy offset path.
Stock reads node state and signed size, copies payload, then loads next at +0x8.
Stock decompilation corroborates unchecked next traversal and payload copy.
Stock decompilation corroborates direct cursor dereference and size-derived copy.

inferences: Because the FIFO pages are exposed by the stock mapping, a writable mapper can race or alter the node metadata consumed by these kernel paths.

An invalid next pointer can cause kernel dereference outside the FIFO allocation; malformed size/cursor values can cause invalid copy lengths or kernel faults. This is a static risk analysis, not a reproduced exploit.
unknowns: No runtime reproduction, exploitability assessment, or user-space permission policy is available.
scope: Richtap shared FIFO used by richtap_update_fifo_data and richtap_rtp_work; offline NX809J stock evidence only.
